title: Preventing a Future Incident where GCE Examination Scripts are Lost or Damaged
what_it_is: Preventing a Future Incident where GCE Examination Scripts are Lost or Damaged

sections.label: GCE script safety and e-marking
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Education about plans for script safety, electronic marking timelines, and preventing lost or stolen scripts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education what are the Ministry's plans in ensuring the safety and integrity of our GCE examination scripts that are sent to the United Kingdom or other overseas marking centres.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry has considered having the GCE "O" and "A" Level exams be e-exams where students key in answers via the computer, or to have written answer scripts be scanned and graded electronically so as to avoid situations of loss or tampering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the timeline for the Ministry's plans to introduce electronic marking of GCE "O" and "A" Level examination scripts and whether the plans will be brought forward; (b) what action is the Ministry taking to prevent a recurrence of stolen or lost scripts including any mitigation action to be taken now pending any change of marking methods in future.

sections.label: GCE answer script numbers
sections.summary: About 1.1 million GCE answer scripts are generated yearly, with 300,000 marked locally and 800,000 marked by Cambridge Assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Each year, there are about 1.1 million answer scripts generated in the GCE Level examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Three hundred thousand answer scripts are marked locally in Singapore while 800,000 answer scripts are marked by Cambridge Assessment.

sections.label: On-screen marking percentage
sections.summary: Close to 65% of all GCE Level written scripts were marked on-screen already.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, close to 65% of all GCE Level written scripts were marked on-screen already.

sections.label: Electronic marking risks study
sections.summary: Going electronic eliminates lost scripts but brings new data risks, so any future system needs careful study and risk mitigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Going electronic will eliminate the risk of lost scripts, but new risks associated with electronic data will surface.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, whatever system we adopt in future, we need to study the pros and cons carefully, proceed methodically, identify and ensure that risks are managed and mitigated to the greatest extent possible.

sections.label: Cambridge markers and local capability
sections.summary: Cambridge Assessment hired 2,200 markers; Singapore has local marking capability but needs 2,200 additional markers within the examination-to-results timeframe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As I mentioned, Cambridge Assessment hired 2,200 markers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have the capability to do all the markings locally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But considering that between examinations and release of results, it is of a certain time frame, 2,200 additional markers are required.

sections.label: Lost scripts from mistaken bag
sections.summary: A bag was left behind, someone mistook the bag, and 32 scripts were lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: A bag was left behind and someone mistook the bag and he lost 32 scripts.

sections.label: Electronic marking and Cambridge collaboration
sections.summary: The question may be moot as marking moves to electronic, which removes lost-script risks but adds new ones, and raises the deeper question of collaboration with Cambridge Assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, the question may well be moot because by the end of this year, we will have substantially moved everything to electronic marking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But as I mentioned earlier, moving away from scripts, you will eliminate the risks of losing scripts but moving to electronic marking, a new set of risks will surface.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think the deeper question is this collaboration with Cambridge Assessment.

sections.label: Keeping Cambridge collaboration worthwhile
sections.summary: Cambridge helped raise Singapore to international repute over many years, so the collaboration is still worthwhile keeping while mitigating the risks of lost scripts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Many, many years of working with them, Cambridge helped us, raised us to this level of international repute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, I think it is a collaboration that is still worthwhile keeping while mitigating the risks of lost scripts.
